scope: The combined private workflow candidate now includes customer planning, prerequisite links, tracker backup inspection, source and findings workbenches, and scanned-page queues. Coding and candidate-specific native Windows and final Linux checks are recorded as complete. The same-host sandbox validator still fails its base-image freshness rule, and there is no independent-review verdict. Separate clean-machine first use, acceptance and release remain open. Prerequisite snapshot comparison and the workspace scanned-page dashboard are now in progress. New work uses native execution; Docker and Windows Sandbox are deferred. No public product download is available.

items.title: Records and evidence foundations
items.detail: Records requests, response gaps, evidence search, source provenance and versioned dossier components are implemented in private development.

items.title: PDF review and correction workflow
items.detail: Source-page citations, explicit match and unread states, a correction round and preserved earlier revisions are implemented in the fictional pilot.

items.title: Combined Windows pilot
items.detail: Usability, packaging, source-wording and startup changes are combined in one candidate. Its recorded Windows suite completed with 6,332 tests passed and 424 skipped.

items.title: Installed Windows journey
items.detail: The final candidate completed 484 installed tests, with three skipped, 13 smoke checks and 281 browser checks. These are automated results on the development machine.

items.title: Reproducible package
items.detail: Two builds of the final fictional pilot produced identical package bytes. Installation and package identity were checked on the development machine.

items.title: First-use rehearsal on a development machine
items.detail: The corrected candidate's package was unpacked, set up and checked in a new folder on a development machine, using fictional records only. The package checks, the one correction round and both recipient checks passed. A separate clean machine and participant feedback are still open, so this is not the clean-machine first use below, an acceptance result or a release.

items.title: Windows verification of the repaired candidate
items.detail: Checked on Windows, on a development machine; not acceptance or release. The final repair round's full Windows test suite completed with 6,686 tests passed, 458 skipped and 0 failed. The candidate carries the repairs: explicit platform skips for the 9 Windows-only file-access cases (they still run on Windows), portable checks for the 2 shell cases, an opaque footer strip in the review bundle's page images that also handles an annotation below a page's crop box and a crop box larger than the media box (a partial fix: an annotation that crosses the bottom edge of a page's visible area remains open; a documented limit remains: the text layer still includes text that a page hides outside its visible area), output-path boundary fixes for transcript-anchor output and '..' handling, now also at 4 further path sites, delivery checks that recognise the same folder however a path is spelled (through folder links or '..'), checked on Windows and not yet confirmed on Linux, review-bundle stamps, highlights and notes placed on rotated pages where the original shows them, except a free-text note that has no drawn appearance, evidence health checks and searches that only read and report that there is nothing to check when there is no database, and a check script that keeps the test run's temporary files in a folder of its own and removes it. The lint and security checks add no new findings (see the baseline item below), the dependency audit found 0 known vulnerabilities, and 209 of 209 deliberately introduced faults were caught by the tests. The package rebuilt twice with identical bytes and installed offline; the smoke test passed 13 of 13 checks, 571 installed tests passed (61 skipped), the headed-browser acceptance run passed 281 checks with 0 failed, and the recipient-route checks passed. The cleanup check that failed in the previous round now passes: the optional installed test run no longer leaves a temporary folder behind. No independent review of the repairs has been run.

items.title: Windows verification of the business evaluation version
items.detail: Checked on Windows, on a development machine; not acceptance or release. The business evaluation version adds capacity profiles (named document limits, offered only once tested), a separate customer installation package, an updated operator guide and a fixed-scope evaluation offer that is still a draft. Its full Windows test suite completed with 8,027 tests passed, 470 skipped and 0 failed. The deliberately introduced faults were caught by the tests (538 of 538). The standard package rebuilt twice with identical bytes and installed offline on a development machine, and the separate customer package, assembled from a fixed list of files, was installed offline, used, stopped and uninstalled there (not on a clean machine). Document limits for the larger evaluation profile were measured on the real code, and that profile is offered only up to the limits that were measured. The evaluation offer is a draft only: it has not been sent or offered to anyone, and no software has been handed out. No independent review of this version has been run. The Linux confirmation is recorded in the next item. A first use on a clean machine is still open.

items.title: Partial Linux verification of the business evaluation version
items.detail: Checked in a Linux container on a development machine; not acceptance or release. The business evaluation version, which carries the repairs of the repaired candidate, ran 138 of its 170 registered test files on Linux, with 6,135 tests passed, 334 skipped and 0 failed. The other 32 files test file-access features that exist only on Windows and run only there, so this is a partial platform check and not a substitute for the Windows suite. The 11 known failures of the earlier Linux run (9 Windows-only file-access cases and 2 shell-portability cases) no longer occur. A reduced set of the deliberately introduced faults was also run on Linux, and all 81 were caught by the tests. The Linux container was shut down afterwards. No independent review of this version has been run. The one open case of the footer-strip fix, a first use on a clean machine and the owner decisions on acceptance and release remain open.

items.title: Checked: customer package builder reliability fixes
items.detail: Checked on Windows, on a development machine; not acceptance or release. A newer version of the business evaluation version fixes reliability problems in the customer package builder's own checks (its output printed every line ending twice, and a check that gets no answer, or a damaged list of the files to ship, ended in a crash report instead of a clear refusal) and adds a test that the start-up refuses an experimental document profile. Its full Windows test suite completed with 8,055 tests passed, 471 skipped and 0 failed. The deliberately introduced faults were caught by the tests (563 of 563, plus 4 of 4 skip checks). The customer package rebuilt twice with identical bytes and was installed, used, stopped and uninstalled on a development machine (59 of 59 checks; not a clean machine). The larger evaluation profile was measured again on this version (20 of 20 runs as required). A partial Linux check in a container on the same development machine ran 138 of the 170 registered test files, with 6,162 tests passed, 336 skipped and 0 failed; the other 32 files test file-access features that exist only on Windows and run only there, so this is a partial platform check and not a substitute for the Windows suite. A reduced set of the deliberately introduced faults was also run on Linux, and all 81 were caught by the tests. The Linux container was shut down afterwards. No independent review of this version has been run. Still open: a first use on a clean machine and the owner decisions on acceptance and release. No software has been handed out.

items.title: Public project presentation
items.detail: This website and its public roadmap are hosted online. Product source and private research remain separate.

items.title: Combined private workflow implementation
items.detail: The private candidate now combines customer planning and prerequisite links, feedback history, private tracker backup inspection, preparation and findings workbenches, delivered-source navigation, and scanned-page work queues. Coding and integration are complete for this checkpoint. Recorded source results remain separate from factual conclusions, and planning records do not approve or release software.

items.title: Checked: combined Windows and Linux candidate
items.detail: The 19 October checkpoint records 12,287 Windows regression checks passed, 497 skipped and none failed, with later affected checks rerun after test and tool changes. The final Linux check passed 9,526 tests with 445 skipped and none failed; 40 registered files were omitted for documented Windows-only behaviour. Windows package, installer, installed smoke and self-check, 281 browser checks, 99 fictional journey scenarios, and uninstall checks also passed on the candidate or its unchanged shipped files. The browser journeys cover the demonstration matter, not the new backup or queue pages. These results are candidate-specific technical checks, not acceptance or release.

items.title: Final technical review
items.detail: The one planned review and one correction pass have been used. The combined candidate has machine checks, but no independent reviewer verdict. Existing review history remains part of the private evidence; machine checks do not replace an independent verdict.

items.title: Business evaluation: acceptance still open
items.detail: The combined private candidate has passed the recorded Windows and final Linux checks described under Completed. Its larger evaluation profile stays within the limits already measured. The separate clean-machine first-use check and owner acceptance and release decisions remain open. The same-host sandbox validator failed its base-image freshness rule; passed test steps do not turn that verdict into a pass. No software has been handed out and no public product download is available.

items.title: In progress: Path safety for workspace folders on Windows
items.detail: The safeguard for long workspace folder paths on Windows has been made on a development copy of the pilot: the pilot now says plainly, before any work starts, when a workspace folder is too long for the default Windows limit of 260 characters, and it cleans up only the leftover temporary folders that it can prove it created itself. A simulation of Linux on the development machine showed that 12 of the new tests failed when run as on Linux because of how those tests were set up, so the tests were corrected; the pilot itself was not changed. On the corrected version the full Windows checks completed on the development machine: the test suite ran with 8,302 tests passed, 471 skipped and 0 failed, and 563 of 563 deliberately introduced faults were caught by the tests. Its first-use run in an isolated, offline Windows sandbox on the development machine ran the full 80-step plan: 78 steps passed, 2 did not apply and none failed; it covered offline setup, the fictional matter journey, the refusals for workspace folders that are too long, a delivery from a folder within the limit, a run stopped part-way on purpose, and uninstalling. Its Linux test run in a container on the development machine ran 139 of 171 test files, with 6,305 tests passed, 370 skipped and 0 failed; the other 32 files test behaviour that exists only on Windows, and 90 of 90 deliberately introduced faults were caught on Linux. On the version before the correction, two sandbox attempts did not finish and one failed a leftover-folder check that the test kit had not expected; only the test kit was corrected. A run stopped part-way can still leave a temporary working folder behind; the install guide documents this and the safeguard does not remove it. These runs used fictional data only and ran on the same machine and Windows build as the development work, and the sandbox guest wrote its own receipts, so this is not a separate clean machine. The change has had no independent review, and none of this is acceptance or release.

items.title: Lint and security baseline
items.detail: The changed-file security checks passed at the combined checkpoint, including dependency audits with no known vulnerabilities in the eight checked manifests. Existing repository-wide formatting, security and secret-scan findings remain; the entire repository is not claimed clean.

items.title: In progress: Automatic local tool startup and shutdown
items.detail: The shared runtime is implemented to start local tools when an operation needs them and close connections, temporary containers and ports after the last active owner finishes. Qualification is in progress, including interrupted jobs. Pilot acceptance and release remain open.

items.title: Windows installer: verification limits remain
items.detail: The private installer built twice with identical output and passed its package verification and 51-check fictional demonstration. Native install, smoke, browser and uninstall checks passed for the candidate's unchanged shipped files. In the same-host Windows sandbox, 48 planned steps passed, 2 did not apply and none failed, but the validator verdict remains FAIL because the base image was older than the host boot. This is not a separate clean machine. Independent review and distribution decisions remain open; the installer has not been handed out.

items.title: Integrated: customer requests and future versions
items.detail: The local tracker records feedback, acceptance criteria, coding briefs, planned versions and operator-recorded deliveries. Saving a record does not run code, verify a release, publish software or contact a customer. This implementation is included in the combined private checkpoint; acceptance and release remain open.

items.title: Integrated: earlier chronology capacity refusal
items.detail: Preparation stops before reading later PDFs once fully prepared documents exceed the existing 1,024 dated-entry ceiling. The crossing document is still fully read, and the recorded count remains a lower bound for the whole matter. This implementation is included in the combined private checkpoint; acceptance and release remain open.

items.title: Integrated: transcript anchors in the local interface
items.detail: The interface can create a transcript anchor using the existing command-line writer. This does not establish the accuracy of the transcript. This implementation is included in the combined private checkpoint; acceptance and release remain open.

items.title: Integrated: customer planning workspace
items.detail: Request search, status, priority and version filters, pagination, planned-version edits and private planning briefs are integrated. Original feedback and customer references stay out of brief downloads by default, and released versions remain locked. This implementation is included in the combined private checkpoint; acceptance and release remain open.

items.title: Integrated: preparation attempts and safe recovery
items.detail: Retained incomplete preparation attempts have a bounded view, explicit Not delivered details, safe links to the existing check-and-prepare flow and a sanitized local diagnostic. Unknown outcomes remain distinct from known failures; there is no automatic retry, deletion or cancellation. This implementation is included in the combined private checkpoint; acceptance and release remain open.

items.title: Integrated: planning triage and version handoff
items.detail: Version search, filters, pagination, target-version reassignment previews, conflict checks, triage and current-scope comparison are integrated. Private downloads do not publish software or contact a customer. This implementation is included in the combined private checkpoint; acceptance and release remain open.

items.title: Integrated: frozen version plans and scope changes
items.detail: Bounded version-plan snapshots can be checked and compared with current recorded scope. Incomplete or stale comparisons are refused. Original feedback and customer references are excluded; an uploaded snapshot is not authenticated history or implementation evidence. This implementation is included in the combined private checkpoint; acceptance and release remain open.

items.title: Integrated: customer planning across platforms
items.detail: The planning component is separated from Windows document services and included in the recorded final Linux checks, while its Windows application integration is preserved. The Windows document-processing offer is unchanged. This implementation is included in the combined private checkpoint; acceptance and release remain open.

items.title: Integrated: source navigator for delivered revisions
items.detail: Delivered revisions have bounded source-inventory and citation browsing, recorded chronology and correction-round comparison. Original records are unchanged and recorded source information remains separate from current verification. This implementation is included in the combined private checkpoint; acceptance and release remain open.

items.title: Integrated: feedback follow-ups and planning history
items.detail: New feedback can link to an earlier request; later planning changes and private local history downloads are retained. Earlier events are not invented, and recorded planning history is not independent evidence. This implementation is included in the combined private checkpoint; acceptance and release remain open.

items.title: Integrated: recovery of unsaved form drafts
items.detail: Refused edits retain submitted request and release-form text beside current saved values, with a private draft download. Drafts are not automatically merged, saved or released. This implementation is included in the combined private checkpoint; acceptance and release remain open.

items.title: Integrated: matter-preparation workbench
items.detail: The integrated workbench provides a searchable matter list, saved-scope comparison, checked-folder filters that retain blockers, a correction-folder preview, bundle-order explanation and private preparation summaries. The existing checks remain the authority. This implementation is included in the combined private checkpoint; acceptance and release remain open.

items.title: Integrated: customer prerequisite planning
items.detail: Explicit prerequisite links, cycle refusal, affected-request views, version context, reassignment previews and private prerequisite briefs are integrated. Prerequisites remain advisory and do not automatically change request status, version scope or release records. This implementation is included in the combined private checkpoint; acceptance and release remain open.

items.title: Integrated: findings and correction workbench
items.detail: Recorded statements and expected-record results have bounded lists, item pages, conservative revision comparisons and private correction briefs. These views do not rerun quotation checks, establish truth or alter evidence. This implementation is included in the combined private checkpoint; acceptance and release remain open.

items.title: Integrated: private tracker backup and recovery guidance
items.detail: The integrated tracker can produce a consistent complete private backup and inspect its format and compatibility before manual recovery. Feedback, links and planning history remain private data. The backup flow does not overwrite a live tracker or upload records. Route, model and application checks passed; a sealed browser journey for these pages remains to be added.

items.title: Integrated: scanned-page work queue and transcript navigation
items.detail: Matter and document queues show recorded page states, retain filters through page navigation, preserve entered fields after a refused action, link exact delivered transcript references, and offer a private selected-work summary. Focused and full-application checks passed on the combined candidate. Existing OCR and individual confirmation rules remain authoritative; the sealed browser journey for these pages is still missing.

items.title: In progress: prerequisite snapshots and comparison
items.detail: Extend private version-plan snapshots and comparison to include prerequisite context while preserving the existing tracker schema and advisory planning boundary. Add native coverage for the current workflow. The assigned work has started in its development workspace. This work uses native checks. Docker and Windows Sandbox are deferred to a later checkpoint. Coding and new execution results are not yet complete.

items.title: In progress: workspace scanned-page work dashboard
items.detail: Add a bounded read-only view across matters with explicit partial, busy and unavailable states and exact links into existing queues. Add the missing native queue, recovery and private-summary browser journey, including keyboard and accessibility checks. The assigned work has started in its development workspace. This work uses native checks. Docker and Windows Sandbox are deferred to a later checkpoint. Coding and new execution results are not yet complete.

items.title: Package a small offline evidence checker
items.detail: Planned, not started: define the smallest source and dependency boundary, check provenance and notices, then package one repeatable fictional example using existing checks. The proposed milestone expands this to three fictional document packs with at least 12 documented checks, expected results, installation guidance and recorded Windows/Linux runs. The scoped component is intended for open source after its licence and publication terms are agreed. The wider platform remains private; no product download is available.

items.title: Finish verifying the repaired candidate
items.detail: What remains: the one open case of the footer-strip fix; and owner decisions on acceptance and release. Results will be recorded here only after they exist; none of this is acceptance or release.

items.title: Verify workspace path safety on a successor candidate
items.detail: The corrected version of the path-safety change has been through the full Windows checks, the first-use run in an isolated, offline Windows sandbox and the Linux test run in a container on the development machine, and its results are recorded under Acceptance still open. It has had no independent review, and none of this is acceptance or release.

items.title: Clean-machine first use
items.detail: Verify the accepted final package on a separate clean machine and record its first-use journey.

items.title: Guided fictional evaluations
items.detail: Use fictional samples with evaluation partners to learn where onboarding, source inspection and revision review can improve.

items.title: Prepare a runnable release
items.detail: Close the remaining technical and release obligations before offering a public product download.
